title: Use secretsx crate for all secret retrieval
description:
Replace all direct secret loading (signing key from file, credentials from env/file) with the secretsx crate once it exists and is published on crates.io.

Why this issue exists:
Today the operator signing key is loaded by hand in server_stores.rs (load_or_generate_signing_key), credentials are loaded from bcrypt files, and there is no abstraction over where secrets come from. For AWS Marketplace deployments, secrets should come from Secrets Manager or KMS. secretsx provides a URI-driven backend-agnostic abstraction that makes this a config change rather than a code change.

Scope:
- Replace load_or_generate_signing_key with a SecretStore::from_uri call; URI configured in [operator] section
- Replace credential file loading with SecretStore-backed retrieval where the backend is a URI
- Wire AwsKmsBackend as the SigningBackend for production deployments (key never leaves KMS)
- Update all four daemon configs (transit, reader, mail, smtp) to accept secret URIs
- Update RUNBOOK.md with Secrets Manager and KMS setup steps for AWS Marketplace deployments

Out of scope:
- Writing secretsx itself (separate project, see SPEC-crate-secretsx.md)
- Migrating existing bcrypt credential stores to a secrets manager (operator's choice)

Acceptance criteria:
- Operator signing key can be configured as secretsx://aws-sm/... or secretsx://aws-kms/... or secretsx://file/... with no code changes
- All secret URIs default to secretsx://file/... or secretsx://env/... so existing deployments are unaffected
- No secret bytes appear in logs or tracing spans
- Integration tests pass with secretsx://file// and secretsx://env/ backends
